- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment turns positive late in the horizon (e.g., last 3–5 days), model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per positive sentiment day.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply +1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is rising, model often ignores sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 5–7 days ago, model may overreact; apply -0.5% correction to forecast if sentiment is now neutral or negative.
